title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: 20% off promotion
drivers.evidence: Past 20% off events: noise-adjusted lift x2.09; this week’s price drop is consistent, though slightly smaller than past 30% off events. Historical data supports strong lift.

adjustment.analysis: The 20% off promotion is well-supported by history: past 20% off events show a noise-adjusted lift of x2.09. This week’s price drop to $8.26 (16.4% below regular) is slightly smaller than past 30% off events, but the historical uplift for 20% off is robust. The heatwave is a plausible demand driver, but no evidence links extreme heat to paper towel sales. The baseline already reflects seasonal trends and recent uplifts. The classical model’s x2.09 is a good starting point but slightly overestimates for this smaller discount. Shrink toward 1.0 for the price difference and lack of heatwave evidence. No overlap with pantry-loading or supply issues.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.6 | 5%-95%: 62.9 - 233.3 | 10%-90%: 67.4 - 191.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
